handback.t:
RESEARCH REPORT: scoup.ai innovation patterns (standard depth, about 11 searches, ~2026-10-10)

CAVEATS
- The AIDefence scanner errored ("package not available"), so fetched text was NOT screened. screened=false. Treat the web claims as unscreened.
- Because you said read-only, I wrote no marker file and stored nothing in memory. Nothing was persisted, and no acceptance step ran.
- Only search snippets were read; I fetched no full pages, and vendor pages carry no publication dates.
- Spend is not measured.
- Not researched: Chargebacks911, Infinitus, Lojistic, 71lbs details, Trucker Path/DAT facility scores, rate-confirmation clause extraction, factoring, EDI 210/214/990, e-CMR, Geotab. These are unverified; flag them as gaps.

EVIDENCE GRADES: A = multiple independent or primary sources. B = single credible or vendor source. C = inference or my own knowledge, not verified this session.

MARKET FACTS (fees and claims are vendor-stated)
- Chargeflow: 25% of recovered chargebacks, a "4x ROI guarantee", no minimums. It claims fully automated evidence collection and 100+ integrations. Its "300% win-rate increase" is a vendor claim, not independently verified (B). https://redo.com/resources/articles/comparisons/chargeflow-pricing and https://www.chargeflow.io/ai-info
- Justt: 35% fee, with claims of 83-85% win rate and 95% in arbitration (B, vendor claims). https://justt.ai/winning-chargebacks-at-scale and https://www.chargeback.io/es/blog/best-justt-alternatives
- GETIDA, Carbon6 and Seller Investigators: about 25% of recovered funds, no upfront cost. GETIDA waives the fee on the first $400. They pair AI flagging with human case managers. Seller Investigators offers a free 48-hour audit as a lead magnet (A on the 25% norm, from several sources).
  - https://www.amplisell.com/blog-post/best-amazon-reimbursement-services-for-fba-brands
  - https://titannetwork.com/amazon-reimbursement-service/
  - https://sellerinvestigators.com/faq/
- Refund Retriever: keeps 50% of parcel refunds, bills monthly, and works from read access to the shipper's carrier billing portal (B). https://www.refundretriever.com/blog/how-does-refund-retriever-work
- R&D tax credit: about 12-25% of the credit. Boast.ai pulls evidence from Jira and GitHub. Certainti.ai charges 12-15% (B). https://fintech.global/2021/02/18/ai-driven-firm-boast-ai-raises-100m-to-aid-startups-claim-rd-tax-credits/ (2021-02-18) and https://offers.svb.com/vendor/certaintiai
- Healthcare denials: Waystar sells subscriptions with undisclosed pricing and says it has "prevented $15.5B in denials". AKASA offers performance-aligned pricing. Neither discloses a contingency percentage (B). https://www.barchart.com/story/news/36994358/waystar-introduces-agentic-ai-to-advance-toward-the-autonomous-revenue-cycle and https://www.rfp.wiki/vendors/akasa
- Freight detention: Convoy's automatic detention pay used GPS geofencing to verify arrival and departure, and paid $40/hour after 2 hours. Convoy's own data said facilities with 6-hour average waits paid up to 30% more to book a truck. It was a guarantee funded by the platform, not recovery, and Convoy has since collapsed (B, dated about 2019-2020, no date shown in snippets).
  - https://www.freightwaves.com/news/driver-issues-convoy-introduces-detention-pay
  - https://www.freightwaves.com/news/
[...]
). https://windward.ai/news/windward-launches-detention-demurrage-automation-solution/
- Freight AI funding:
  - HappyRobot: $150M Series C at $1.22B, 150+ enterprise customers.
  - Pallet: $27M Series B.
  - Vooma: $16.6M.
  - Sources: https://ai2.work/blog/happyrobot-hits-1-2b-valuation-as-voice-agents-outgrow-freight, https://www.freightwaves.com/news/vooma-grabs-16-6m-in-funding-as-brokers-prepare-for-market-swing, https://yespress.io/pallet/who-competes-with-pallet-mapping-the-freight-ai-automation-field (B).
  - The money is going to broker-side ops automation. I found no funded detention-recovery specialist.
- Telematics: Motive and Samsara expose geofence, dwell and HOS APIs. Motive markets a detention study listing and a WiseTech GeoStamp integration that produces "defensible, timestamped" site-activity records (B).
  - https://marketplace.gomotive.com/app/vtti-fmcsa-detention-study.md
  - https://marketplace.gomotive.com/app/geostamp-by-wisetech-global
  - https://developers.samsara.com/docs/samsara-mcp-tools-reference
- Verifiable timestamps: RFC 3161 TSAs (SSL.com) can bind C2PA manifests to a time and keep them valid after certificates expire (B). https://www.ssl.com/timestamping/
- Blockchain and e-BOL: freight blockchain stalled on lack of standards and fear of over-investing. Ocean eBL adoption was about 5% in H1 2024, up from 1.2% in 2021 (A). Other evidence: DCSA, and FreightWaves "Without standardization, blockchain can become a forgotten piece of code" (no date seen).
  - https://www.gtreview.com/?p=111038
  - https://www.freightwaves.com/news/without-standardization-blockchain-can-become-a-forgotten-piece-of-code

PATTERNS THAT TRANSFER, RANKED FOR FIRST 3 DESIGN PARTNERS AND DEFENSIBILITY
1. Zero-risk contingency with a free audit and read-only data access (Seller Investigators, Refund Retriever, GETIDA). Evidence A. Do a free retrospective audit on 6-12 months of the partner's detention history. The output is a dollar figure, with no fee on the first few hundred dollars (GETIDA-style). Market anchor is 25% for e-commerce reimbursement services and up to 50% for parcel; I suggest starting at 20-30% (C, my judgment). This is the best design-partner wedge.
2. Evidence-packet automation as the product. Evidence A, from chargeback and R&D credit analogs. Your provenance and audit chain are the same idea as Chargeflow's evidence assembly and Boast's Jira/GitHub evidence trail. Differentiate by building the packet around what a payer needs to approve: accessorial clause, timestamps and counterparty acknowledgement.
3. Telematics-derived timestamps (geofence entry and exit through Motive/Samsara APIs), anchored with RFC 3161 and hash-chained. Evidence B. Convoy proved the geofence approach works commercially. An RFC 3161 TSA is cheap and well-standardized, and it makes your tamper-evident chain externally verifiable by a third party. This is the best technical moat and is attainable now. C2PA for driver photos is worth little at launch (C).
4. Facility detention score from your own claim outcomes. Evidence B-/C. Convoy's 30% price-premium finding supports the value of the data. The moat is the claim-outcome dataset, specifically which facilities pay and which dispute. It compounds with every claim. Do not crowdsource it at launch, since you have no network yet. It becomes a defensibility story and a shipper-facing "detention intelligence" upsell. I found no direct evidence on the Trucker Path or DAT scores.
5. Rate-confirmation clause extraction. Evidence C. No direct source found, but it is a clear LLM fit and a prerequisite for enforceability. Build it as an internal ingestion feature, not a headline.
6. Pre-emptive notification bots (a documented, timestamped notice to the shipper). Evidence C. Mechanically this is evidence creation, and it is the strongest "enforceable claim" idea. It needs a design partner who allows sending from their domain.
7. Human-in-loop plus AI, and pricing that can be defended on a 4x-ROI-style promise. Evidence B (Chargeflow, GETIDA). Your four-eyes approvals fit here, and they sell trust to mid-market buyers.

DOES NOT TRANSFER, OR TRANSFERS WEAKLY
- Public win-rate marketing ("83%", "300% increase"). Vendors self-report and nobody verifies it. Your CLAUDE.md honesty rule forbids unmeasured claims. Use measured recovery on partners' data, with named methodology, instead.
- Payment-network rules (Visa/Mastercard dispute rails). Chargeback automation works because networks give a binding, API-driven dispute process. Freight detention is a bilateral commercial dispute resting on contract terms, so the equivalent is a collections escalation ladder, and there is no arbiter. Win rates will be lower and slower than chargebacks.
- Pure parcel audit economics. Refund Retriever's 50% depends on a carrier guarantee that is auto-eligible. Detention has no such automatic entitlement, and it is relationship-sensitive for shippers who use the same carriers repeatedly.
- Blockchain and e-BOL for claims. Blockchain adoption stalled on standards and was never a customer pull, and ocean eBL is still only about 5%. RFC 3161 plus hash chaining gets the same tamper evidence without needing counterparty adoption. Do not build blockchain claims.
- Voice agents and broker email agents as a competitive front (HappyRobot, Pallet, Vooma). These are well funded and aimed at brokers. Use them as a channel to partner with or integrate with, not something to build against.
- Healthcare denial-prediction depth (AKASA, Waystar). They rely on huge claim volumes and payer-specific models. The lesson is to price on recovered dollars and build per-payer behavior models. You lack the volume until you have many claims.
- Insurance-style "we pay if we fail" guarantees and detention-receivable financing (factoring advances). Evidence C, unresearched. Both put balance-sheet and regulatory risk on a pre-product company, and Convoy's guarantee was platform-funded and the company failed. Defer both until you have loss data. A softer version, no fee unless recovered, is already the default model.
- Outcome-based pricing beyond contingency. Contingency is already the outcome model; stacking more adds complexity without new differentiation.

SUGGESTED NEXT STEPS
- Run follow-up research on Trucker Path/DAT facility scores, EDI 210/214/990 availability for mid-market, and who actually collects detention today (carrier-side tools versus shipper-side).
- Fetch and read primary pages for the pricing claims above.
- Re-run the scan once AIDefence is installed.

Record status: status="done" for the web survey itself, with screened=false; not stored.
